definition: The process of obtaining explicit permission from users before storing or accessing cookies on their devices, as required by privacy regulations like GDPR and similar laws.
metaDescription: Learn about cookie consent requirements, how websites must ask permission before storing cookies, and your rights to control tracking.
simpleExplanation: Cookie consent is when websites ask for your permission before placing tracking files on your device. Those pop-up banners asking to "Accept All Cookies" or letting you customize preferences are cookie consent mechanisms required by law.
whyItMatters: Cookie consent gives you control over your digital privacy by letting you decide what data websites can collect about you. Without proper consent, companies could track your online behavior without your knowledge or permission.
technicalDetail: Cookie consent mechanisms must meet legal requirements including granular controls for different cookie categories, clear opt-out options, and documentation of user choices. Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and easily withdrawable under regulations like GDPR Article 7.

examples.explanation: A news site shows a banner with options to accept all cookies, reject non-essential cookies, or customize preferences for analytics, advertising, and functional cookies separately.
An online store provides a detailed cookie settings page where you can toggle different types of tracking on/off and see exactly what data each cookie type collects.
A blog asks for consent before loading YouTube videos or Facebook comments, since these embeds would place third-party tracking cookies on your device.
